audit: The records-office analogy names retention and exceptions without making a reader inspect how the same deletion request yields different lawful handling under a verified hold. Lesson A follows one record through live copies, backup obligations and a narrowly scoped hold; neither branch claims instantaneous universal erasure. Lesson B pairs three audit claims with concrete receipts, exposing the gap between a readable hash chain and integrity anchored outside the writer's control. The exercise also challenges an unsupported backup-erasure claim. Both lessons separate evidence from assurance and retain the chapter's distinctions among minimization, purpose, access, integrity and recordkeeping obligations without prescribing universal retention periods.

lessons.title: One deletion request, two retention conditions
lessons.intro: Record C-7 appears in live state, a derived evaluation sample and backups. A verified deletion request arrives. Compare handling with no applicable hold against a verified hold covering C-7.

data.input: Delete C-7 and derived copies under the applicable policy.

left.title: No applicable hold
steps: Locate live and derived copies by lineage
Schedule backup expiry and restore suppression
left.result: Live deletion confirmed; backup expiration remains pending

right.title: Verified scoped hold
steps: Validate hold H-3 covers C-7 and its purpose
Restrict held copies; delete eligible extras
Record deferred deletion and next hold review
right.result: Covered records retained under hold, with controlled access

read: Both paths start with the same record lineage and verified request.
The hold changes which copies are currently eligible for deletion.
Neither live deletion nor a hold proves all backup copies disappeared.
lessons.question: May the no-hold path report immediate deletion from all backups?
lessons.answer: No. Its stated contract provides scheduled backup expiry and prevents deleted data from returning through restores. It must report that timing accurately rather than equating live-store deletion with universal immediate erasure.
lessons.takeaway: Deletion follows lineage, eligibility and each storage contract.
lessons.assumption: Fictional retention policy; verified holds and backup schedules are organization-specific. No universal legal rule or deletion deadline is implied.

lessons.title: Which audit claims do these receipts support?
lessons.intro: A reviewer inspects three claims about C-7. The receipts are deliberately narrow: a live-delete acknowledgement, a writer-controlled hash-chain check, and a protected external checkpoint digest.

claims.text: C-7 was removed from the live state store.
C-7 was erased immediately from every backup.
The export matches the externally retained digest.

sources.text: Live-state receipt: C-7 delete committed at 14:03; 1 row removed.
Local audit chain verifies; writer can replace every event and hash.
Protected checkpoint: export digest 7ac; recomputed export digest 7ac.

data.verdict: Scope every assurance to the copy, event and trust boundary its evidence covers.

read: The live receipt supports one specific store deletion.
A local hash check says nothing about backup deletion.
An independently protected digest helps detect later rewriting of this export.
lessons.question: Does the third receipt prove every original audit event was truthful?
lessons.answer: No. It supports consistency with an independently retained checkpoint. It does not establish truth at event creation, complete lineage, confidentiality or deletion of other copies. Those need their own controls and evidence.
lessons.takeaway: Audit integrity and operational truth require different evidence.
lessons.assumption: Fictional receipts; digest values are abbreviated. The external anchor is outside the writer's control; its protection is an explicit assumption.
